tip: Indonesian verbs never change for -ing – sedang does the job: sedang membaca = in the middle of reading. Drop sedang and it just means 'read'.
No past tense here – sudah bangun is literally 'already wake'. sudah marks the action as finished; the verb bangun itself never changes.
sarapan is a verb all by itself – Saya sarapan roti is literally 'I breakfast bread'. No word for 'have' or 'eat' needed.
pulang packs 'go home' into one word – langsung pulang = head straight home. There is no separate word for 'home' in the sentence.
